title: Help me with this form
goal: At the office, ask Maryam to help you fill in a form in Arabic, using Form III verbs: sāʿdīni 'help me', ḥāwalt 'I tried'
tip: Form III verbs have a long ā after the first letter: sāʿad 'he helped', ḥāwal 'he tried', sāfar 'he travelled'. Past: ḥāwalt 'I tried'. Command: sāʿidni 'help me', to a woman sāʿdīni. 'You helped me' is sāʿadtni, to a woman sāʿadtīni.
grammar: Forms III, V, VI as chunks: Form III past and command (sāʿad, ḥāwal)
dialogue: B
مريم، ساعديني الله يخليج. الاستمارة كلها بالعربي
Maryam, sāʿdīni allāh ykhallīch. il-istimāra killha bil-ʿarabi
Maryam, help me, please. The form's all in Arabic.
A
أكيد. بس حاول أول بروحك، عشان تتعلم
akīd. bas ḥāwil awwal b-rūḥak, ʿashān titʿallam
Of course. But try on your own first, so you learn.
B
حاولت والله! بس ما فهمت هالكلمة
ḥāwalt wallāh! bas ma fhimt hal-kilma
I did try, honestly! But I didn't understand this word.
A
هذي يعني تاريخ ميلادك. اكتب هني
hādhi yaʿni tārīkh mīlādak. iktib hni
This means your date of birth. Write it here.
B
زين. وهني شو أكتب؟
zēn. w hni shu aktib?
OK. And what do I write here?
A
هني اسمك بس. وخلاص، عبيتها!
hni ismak bas. w khalāṣ, ʿabbēt-ha!
Just your name here. And that's it, you've filled it in!
B
والله ساعدتيني وايد. مشكورة!
wallāh sāʿadtīni wāyid. mashkūra!
Honestly, you've been a big help. Thanks!
A
العفو. وإذا تبي شي ثاني، أنا موجودة
il-ʿafu. w idha tabi shay thāni, ana mawjūda
You're welcome. And if you need anything else, I'm here.
items: to a woman: sāʿadtīni (ساعدتيني); the same spelling read sāʿdatni means 'she helped me'
I tried; you tried (to a man)
to a woman: ḥāwli (حاولي); ḥāwil awwal b-rūḥak = try on your own first
you filled it in (to a man); I filled it in
to a woman (you filled it in): ʿabbētīha (عبيتيها); to fill in: yʿabbi (يعبي)
to a woman: iktibi hni (اكتبي هني)
I'm here (if you need me), I'm around (a man)

title: At the service counter
goal: Ask a clerk at a service counter about your paperwork, using Form III verbs in the present: agābil 'I see (someone)', baḥāwil 'I'll try'
tip: Form III keeps its long ā in the present: agābil 'I meet, I see (someone)', asāʿdak 'I help you', arājiʿ 'I check back (at an office)'. Future: baḥāwil 'I'll try', batābiʿ 'I'll follow (it) up'. The past has it too: sāfar 'he's gone away' (you know sāfart).
grammar: Forms III, V, VI as chunks: Form III present (agābil, baḥāwil, arājiʿ)
dialogue: A
تفضل، عندك موعد؟
tfaẓẓal, ʿindak mawʿid?
Yes, go ahead. Do you have an appointment?
B
لا، بس أبي أقابل المدير عن معاملتي
la, bas abi agābil il-mudīr ʿan muʿāmalti
No, but I'd like to see the manager about my paperwork.
A
المدير سافر هالأسبوع. بس بحاول أساعدك
il-mudīr sāfar hal-usbūʿ. bas baḥāwil asāʿdak
The manager's away this week. But I'll try to help you.
B
الله يخليك. معاملتي صار لها شهر
allāh ykhallīk. muʿāmalti ṣār-lha shahar
Thank you. My application's been waiting a month.
A
عطني رقم المعاملة... هيه، عند المدير. لازم يوقعها هو
ʿaṭni ragam il-muʿāmala... hē, ʿind il-mudīr. lāzim ywaggiʿha huwa
Give me the application number... Yes, it's with the manager. He has to sign it himself.
B
ما قصرت. يعني أراجع بعد ما يرجع؟
mā gaṣṣart. yaʿni arājiʿ baʿd ma yirjaʿ?
Thanks a lot. So should I come back after he's back?
A
ما سوينا شي. لا تحاتي، أنا بتابعها وبتصل فيك
mā sawwēna shay. la tḥāti, ana batābiʿha w battaṣil fīk
Not at all. Don't worry, I'll follow it up and call you.
B
زين، بترياك
zēn, batrayyāk
Great, I'll wait to hear from you.
items: I'd like to see (someone), I want to meet
agābil = I meet; gābalt (قابلت) = I met
the paperwork, the application (at an office)
my paperwork: muʿāmalti (معاملتي); your paperwork: muʿāmaltak (معاملتك)
baḥāwil asāʿdak = I'll try to help you
hē, ʿind il-mudīr = yes, it's with the manager
your number (to a man): ragmak (رقمك); ragam il-muʿāmala = the application number
I check back, I follow up (at an office)
not arjaʿ (أرجع) 'I come back': arājiʿ is going back to an office about your paperwork
I'll follow it up, I'll keep track of it
culture: At a service counter, say what you need in one line (abi … ʿan muʿāmalti) and thank the clerk with mā gaṣṣart; the answer is mā sawwēna shay. muʿāmala is the everyday word for any paperwork you're waiting on at an office.

title: I met our new neighbour
goal: Tell Sēf about a new neighbour you've got to know, using Form V verbs: tʿarraft ʿala 'I got to know', tkharraj 'he graduated'
tip: Form V is t- + a Form II verb: ʿallam 'taught' → tʿallam 'learned', ʿarraf 'introduced' → tʿarraf ʿala 'got to know'. Past: tʿarraft ʿalēh 'I got to know him', tʿallamt 'I learned', tkharraj 'he graduated'. You already know one: tʿawwadt ʿala.
grammar: Forms III, V, VI as chunks: Form V past (tʿarraf, tkharraj, tʿallam)
dialogue: A
منو هذا اللي كنت تسولف وياه؟
minu hādha illi kint tsōlif wiyyāh?
Who's that you were chatting with?
B
هذا جارنا اليديد. تعرفت عليه أمس
hādha jārna l-yidīd. tʿarraft ʿalēh ams
That's our new neighbour. I got to know him yesterday.
A
حلو! شو يسوي؟ يدرس؟
ḥilu! shu ysawwi? yidris?
Nice! What does he do? Is he a student?
B
لا، تخرج السنة اللي طافت وتوظف في بنك
la, tkharraj is-sana illi ṭāfat w twaẓẓaf fi bank
No, he graduated last year and got a job at a bank.
A
ما شاء الله. وانت تحسنت وايد في العربي!
mā shāʼ allāh. w inta tḥassant wāyid fi l-ʿarabi!
Good for him. And your Arabic's got so much better!
B
تعلمت من الجيران! تعودت عليهم، نسولف كل يوم
tʿallamt min il-jīrān! tʿawwadt ʿalēhum, nsōlif kill yōm
I learned from the neighbours! I've got used to them; we chat every day.
A
زين عيل، خلني أتعرف عليه أنا بعد
zēn ʿayal, khallni atʿarraf ʿalēh ana baʿad
Great, then let me meet him too.
B
أكيد. تعال الخميس ونشرب قهوة ويا بعض
akīd. taʿāl il-khamīs w nishrab gahwa wiyya baʿaẓ
Sure. Come on Thursday and we'll have coffee together.
items: I got to know, I met (someone new); you got to know (to a man)
to a woman (you got to know): tʿarrafti ʿala (تعرفتي على); tʿarraft ʿalēh = I got to know him
let me meet him, I'd like to get to know him
my neighbour: jāri (جاري); UAE also: yār (يار), yārna (يارنا)
you've improved, you've got better (to a man); I've improved
to a woman (you've improved): tḥassanti (تحسنتي); it's got better: tḥassan (تحسن)
I learned; you learned (to a man)

title: Viewing a flat
goal: View a flat with its owner and ask what's included, using Form V verbs in the present: tfarraj 'have a look', batʿawwad 'I'll get used to it'
tip: Form V in the present is yit- / tit- + the doubled verb: titfarraj 'you look around', bititʿawwad 'you'll get used to it'. 'I' has no i: atʿawwad, batʿawwad 'I'll get used to it'. The command has no prefix: tfarraj 'have a look', to a woman tfarraji.
grammar: Forms III, V, VI as chunks: Form V present and command (tfarraj, batʿawwad)
dialogue: A
حياك الله. تفضل، تفرج على الشقة على راحتك
ḥayyāk allāh. tfaẓẓal, tfarraj ʿala sh-shigga ʿala rāḥtak
Welcome. Come in, have a look round the flat, take your time.
B
الله يحييك. ما شاء الله، الشقة واسعة
allāh yḥayyīk. mā shāʼ allāh, ish-shigga wāsʿa
Thank you. Wow, the flat's spacious.
A
غرفتين وصالة، ومفروشة بعد
ghurfatēn w ṣāla, w mafrūsha baʿad
Two bedrooms and a living room, and it's furnished too.
B
زين. والكهربا؟ مع الإيجار؟
zēn. w il-kahraba? maʿa l-ījār?
Good. And the electricity? Is it in the rent?
A
لا، الكهربا والماي عليك. بس المنطقة هادية
la, il-kahraba w il-māy ʿalēk. bas il-manṭiga hādya
No, electricity and water are on you. But the area's quiet.
B
بعيدة شوي عن شغلي. بس بتعوّد إن شاء الله
baʿīda shwayy ʿan shughli. bas batʿawwad in shāʼ allāh
It's a bit far from my work. But I'll get used to it, God willing.
A
أكيد بتتعود. والمترو قريب، خمس دقايق مشي
akīd bititʿawwad. w il-mitrō garīb, khams dagāyig mashi
Of course you will. And the metro's close, five minutes' walk.
B
زين. بفكر وبرد عليك باكر
zēn. bafakkir w barudd ʿalēk bāchir
Great. I'll think about it and get back to you tomorrow.
items: to a woman: tfarraji (تفرجي); you look around: titfarraj (تتفرج)
take your time, as you like (to a man)
to a woman: ʿala rāḥtich (على راحتج)
ghurfatēn w ṣāla = two bedrooms and a living room
you'll get used to it: bititʿawwad (بتتعود)
ʿashr dagāyig mashi = ten minutes' walk
bafakkir w barudd ʿalēk = I'll think about it and get back to you
is it included in the rent?, with the rent?
il-kahraba maʿa l-ījār? = is electricity included in the rent?
culture: Flats are usually described by their rooms: ghurfa w ṣāla is a one-bedroom flat, ghurfatēn w ṣāla a two-bedroom. What the rent covers differs from flat to flat, so ask (maʿa l-ījār?) and read the contract before you agree.

title: We came to an agreement
goal: Tell Sēf how you and the flat's owner sorted things out, using Form VI 'each other' verbs: tlāgēna 'we met up', tfāhamna 'we agreed'
tip: Form VI is t- + a Form III verb, and usually means 'each other', so its subject is mostly plural: tlāgēna 'we met up', tfāhamna 'we came to an agreement', binitfāham 'we'll sort it out'. You know its present already: nitlāga 'we meet up'.
grammar: Forms III, V, VI as chunks: Form VI past and future (tlāgēna, tfāhamna, binitfāham)
dialogue: A
بشّر! شو صار ويا صاحب الشقة؟
bashshir! shu ṣār wiyya ṣāḥib ish-shigga?
So, tell me! What happened with the flat's owner?
B
أبشرك، تلاقينا أمس وتفاهمنا على كل شي
abashshrak, tlāgēna ams w tfāhamna ʿala kill shay
Good news: we met up yesterday and agreed on everything.
A
زين! والإيجار؟ نزل شوي؟
zēn! w il-ījār? nizal shwayy?
Great! And the rent? Did it come down a bit?
B
هيه، نزل شوي. وأنا وربيعي بندفع نص نص
hē, nizal shwayy. w ana w rbīʿi binidfaʿ nuṣṣ nuṣṣ
Yes, a bit. And my friend and I will pay half each.
A
حلو. ومتى بتسكنون فيها؟
ḥilu. w mita bitisknūn fīha?
Nice. And when are you moving in?
B
آخر الشهر. تقدر تساعدنا؟
ākhir ish-shahar. tigdar tsāʿidna?
At the end of the month. Can you help us?
A
أكيد! أنا وفهد. وبنتفاهم على اليوم بعدين
akīd! ana w Fahad. w binitfāham ʿala l-yōm baʿdēn
Of course! Fahad and I will. And we'll sort out the day later.
B
يلا، اتفقنا!
yalla, ittafagna!
Right, deal!
items: we came to an agreement, we sorted it out
tfāhamna ʿala kill shay = we agreed on everything
we'll sort it out, we'll work it out (between us)
the owner of the house: ṣāḥib il-bēt (صاحب البيت)
so, tell me (the news)! (to a man)
to a woman: bashshri (بشري); said when you're waiting for news; the answer starts abashshrak (أبشرك); also bashshirni (بشرني)
I've got good news for you (to a man)
to a woman: abashshrich (أبشرج); the answer to bashshir!
it went down, it came down (a price)
binidfaʿ nuṣṣ nuṣṣ = we'll split it half and half
you'll live, you're moving in (to a group)
to one man: bitiskin (بتسكن); to one woman: bitisknīn (بتسكنين)

title: Opening a bank account
goal: Open a bank account and ask a bank employee about an Islamic account, recycling Forms III and VI
tip: This lesson recycles the derived forms. Form III: asāʿdak 'I help you'. Form VI: tʿāmalt wiyyāna 'you've dealt with us (before)', from tʿāmal 'deal with each other'. With a woman, B says hala fīch and law samaḥti.
dialogue: A
هلا، تفضل. شو أقدر أساعدك؟
hala, tfaẓẓal. shu agdar asāʿdak?
Hello, go ahead. How can I help you?
B
هلا فيج. أبي أفتح حساب، لو سمحتي
hala fīch. abi aftaḥ ḥsāb, law samaḥti
Hello. I'd like to open an account, please.
A
أكيد. تعاملت ويانا من قبل؟
akīd. tʿāmalt wiyyāna min gabil?
Of course. Have you banked with us before?
B
لا، أول مرة. عندكم حساب إسلامي؟
la, awwal marra. ʿindakum ḥsāb islāmi?
No, it's the first time. Do you have an Islamic account?
A
هيه عندنا. تبي حساب توفير ولّا حساب عادي؟
hē ʿindana. tabi ḥsāb tawfīr walla ḥsāb ʿādi?
Yes, we do. Do you want a savings account or a normal one?
B
عادي بس. الشركة تبي حساب بنك عشان الراتب
ʿādi bas. ish-sharika tabi ḥsāb bank ʿashān ir-rātib
Just a normal one. The company wants a bank account for my salary.
A
زين. خذ هالورقة، فيها كل الأوراق اللي لازم تييبها
zēn. khudh hal-warga, fīha kill il-awrāg illi lāzim tyībha
OK. Take this sheet; it lists all the documents you need to bring.
B
زين، بييبها باكر إن شاء الله. ساعدتيني وايد!
zēn, bayībha bāchir in shāʼ allāh. sāʿadtīni wāyid!
Great, I'll bring them tomorrow, God willing. You've been a big help!
items: I'd like to open an account
you've dealt with us, you've been our customer (to a man)
to a woman: tʿāmalti wiyyāna (تعاملتي ويانا)
a current account: ḥsāb jāri (حساب جاري)
this sheet, this piece of paper
culture: Islamic banking is common in the UAE: there are Islamic banks, and many other banks offer Islamic accounts too. If it matters to you, ask ʿindakum ḥsāb islāmi? Each bank sets its own list of documents, so ask the bank for it rather than relying on what a friend needed.

title: You're breaking up!
goal: Phone Sēf from the airport when the line keeps cutting out, using Form VII verbs: ingiṭaʿ 'it cut out', inkisar 'it broke'
tip: Form VII adds in- and says something happened to the thing itself, with nobody named: ingiṭaʿ 'it got cut off', inkisar 'it broke'. For a feminine noun: inkisrat. Present: yingiṭiʿ 'it cuts out': il-khaṭṭ gāʿid yingiṭiʿ 'the line keeps cutting out'.
grammar: Forms VII, VIII, X as chunks: Form VII (ingiṭaʿ, inkisar)
dialogue: A
ألو؟ وينك؟ الخط قاعد ينقطع
alō? wēnak? il-khaṭṭ gāʿid yingiṭiʿ
Hello? Where are you? The line keeps cutting out.
B
أنا في المطار. تسمعني الحين؟
ana fi l-maṭār. tismaʿni l-ḥīn?
I'm at the airport. Can you hear me now?
A
هيه، الحين أحسن. انقطع مرتين!
hē, il-ḥīn aḥsan. ingiṭaʿ marratēn!
Yes, it's better now. It cut out twice!
B
الشبكة هني مب زينة. وتلفوني انكسرت شاشته
ish-shabaka hni mub zēna. w tilifōni inkisrat shāshtah
The network here isn't good. And my phone's screen broke.
A
أفا! كيف انكسرت؟
afa! chēf inkisrat?
Oh no! How did it break?
B
طاح من إيدي في الطيارة
ṭāḥ min īdi fi ṭ-ṭayyāra
It fell out of my hand on the plane.
A
خسارة! زين، أنا ياي. طلعت؟
khasāra! zēn, ana yāy. ṭilaʿt?
What a shame! OK, I'm on my way. Are you out yet?
B
لا، أتريا الشنطة. شكلها ما وصلت!
la, atrayya sh-shanṭa. shaklha ma wiṣlat!
No, I'm waiting for my bag. Looks like it hasn't come!
items: it cut out, it got cut off (a line, the water)
for a feminine noun such as il-kahraba 'the power': ingiṭʿat (انقطعت)
it cuts out, it keeps cutting out
il-khaṭṭ gāʿid yingiṭiʿ = the line keeps cutting out
it fell out of my hand, I dropped it
for a feminine noun: ṭāḥat min īdi (طاحت من إيدي)
oh no!, really? (on hearing bad news)

title: My bag didn't arrive
goal: Report a missing bag at the airport counter, using Form VIII verbs: aḥtāj 'I need', miḥtāj 'in need of'
tip: Form VIII puts -t- after the first letter: iḥtāj 'he needed'. Present: aḥtāj 'I need', tiḥtāj 'you need', to a woman tiḥtājīn. The participle miḥtāj (a woman: miḥtāja) also means 'I need': ana miḥtāj anām 'I need to sleep'.
grammar: Forms VII, VIII, X as chunks: Form VIII present and participle (aḥtāj, tiḥtāj, miḥtāj)
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. شنطتي ما وصلت ويا الطيارة
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. shanṭti ma wiṣlat wiyya ṭ-ṭayyāra
Hello. My bag didn't come on the plane.
A
وعليكم السلام. من وين ياي؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. min wēn yāy?
Hello. Where have you flown in from?
B
من لندن. وكل أغراضي فيها، حتى الهدايا اللي اشتريتها!
min Landan. w kill aghrāẓi fīha, ḥatta l-hadāya illi ishtarēt-ha!
From London. And all my things are in it, even the presents I bought!
A
لا تحاتي. أحتاج رقمك وعنوانك بس
la tḥāti. aḥtāj ragmak w ʿinwānak bas
Don't worry. I just need your number and address.
B
تفضل. ومتى بتوصل؟ أحتاج ملابس
tfaẓẓal. w mita bitōṣal? aḥtāj malābis
Here you go. And when will it get here? I need clothes.
A
يمكن باكر. تحتاج شي الحين؟
yimkin bāchir. tiḥtāj shay il-ḥīn?
Maybe tomorrow. Do you need anything now?
B
لا، بس محتاج أنام. صار لي يوم كامل مسافر!
la, bas miḥtāj anām. ṣār-li yōm kāmil msāfir!
No, I just need to sleep. I've been travelling a whole day!
A
أول ما توصل الشنطة، بنتصل فيك
awwal ma tōṣal ish-shanṭa, binittaṣil fīk
As soon as the bag arrives, we'll call you.
items: do you need anything? (to a man)
to a woman: tiḥtājīn shay? (تحتاجين شي؟)
in need of; I need (a man)
a woman: miḥtāja (محتاجة); ana miḥtāj anām = I need to sleep
my bag didn't arrive, my bag hasn't come
all my things, all my stuff
where have you come from? (to a man)
to a woman: min wēn yāya? (من وين ياية؟)
a whole day, a full day
to a woman: binittaṣil fīch (بنتصل فيج)

title: Back from London
goal: Tell Maryam at work what happened with your lost bag, using Form VIII verbs in the past: ittaṣalt 'I called', ikhtart 'I chose'
tip: Form VIII in the past starts with i-: ittaṣalt 'I called', ishtarēt 'I bought', ikhtart 'I chose', irtaḥt 'I rested'. After ma the i stays: ma ishtarēt. Everyday speech also says shirēt 'I bought' (Form I). To a woman, 'you' adds -ti: ittaṣalti, irtaḥti.
grammar: Forms VII, VIII, X as chunks: Form VIII past (ittaṣalt, ikhtart, irtaḥt)
dialogue: A
الحمد لله على السلامة! متى رجعت؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma! mita rijaʿt?
Welcome back! When did you get back?
B
الله يسلمج. أمس، بس شنطتي ما وصلت
allāh ysallmich. ams, bas shanṭti ma wiṣlat
Thank you. Yesterday, but my bag didn't arrive.
A
أفا! وشو سويت؟
afa! w shu sawwēt?
Oh no! So what did you do?
B
اتصلت فيهم الصبح، وقالوا بتوصل اليوم
ittaṣalt fīhum iṣ-ṣubḥ, w gālaw bitōṣal il-yōm
I called them this morning, and they said it'll arrive today.
A
زين. وملابسك كلها في الشنطة؟
zēn. w malābsak killha fi sh-shanṭa?
Good. And all your clothes are in the bag?
B
هيه! رحت المول وشريت قميصين، ولبست واحد
hē! riḥt il-mōl w shirēt gamīṣēn, w libast wāḥid
Yes! I went to the mall, bought two shirts and put one on.
A
زين سويت! والثاني؟ شو اخترت؟
zēn sawwēt! w ith-thāni? shu ikhtart?
Good thinking! And the other one? What did you go for?
B
أبيض بعد. ونمت عدل وارتحت، الحمد لله
abyaẓ baʿad. w nimt ʿadil w irtaḥt, il-ḥamdu lillāh
White as well. And I slept properly and I'm rested, thank God.
items: I called; you called (to a man)
to a woman (you called): ittaṣalti (اتصلتي); ittaṣalt fīhum = I called them
gālaw bitōṣal = they said it'll arrive
for a masculine thing: biyōṣal (بيوصل); the same form also means 'you'll arrive' (to a man)
I wore, I put on; you wore (to a man)
I chose, I picked; you chose (to a man)
I rested, I feel rested; you rested (to a man)
to a woman (you rested): irtaḥti (ارتحتي); also 'I was relieved'
I slept properly, I slept well
culture: When someone gets back from a trip, say il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma; the answer is allāh ysallmak, to a woman allāh ysallmich.

title: The AC isn't working
goal: Complain at a hotel reception about your room, using Form X verbs: istaghrabt 'I'm surprised', astakhdim 'I use'
tip: Form X adds sta- before the root: istaghrab 'was surprised' (gh-r-b), istakhdam 'used' (kh-d-m). Past: istaghrabt 'I'm surprised'. In the present the i goes: astakhdim 'I use'. istalam 'received' only looks like Form X: it is Form VIII (s-l-m with -t-, like ishtaghal).
grammar: Forms VII, VIII, X as chunks: Form X (istaghrab, istakhdam)
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. استلمنا الغرفة، بس المكيف ما يشتغل
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. istalamna l-ghurfa, bas il-mkayyif ma yishtaghil
Hello. We've got our room, but the AC isn't working.
A
وعليكم السلام. السموحة منك! أي غرفة؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. is-samūḥa minnak! ay ghurfa?
Hello. We're so sorry! Which room?
B
ما عليه. غرفة مية وعشرين
ma ʿalēh. ghurfa miya w ʿishrīn
That's all right. Room one hundred and twenty.
A
استغربت! المكيف في هالغرفة يديد
istaghrabt! il-mkayyif fi hal-ghurfa yidīd
That's strange! The AC in that room is new.
B
والماي الحار بعد انقطع
w il-māy il-ḥārr baʿad ingiṭaʿ
And the hot water's gone off too.
A
ولا يهمك، بطرش لك واحد يشوفهم الحين
wala yhimmak, baṭarrish-lak wāḥid yshūfhum il-ḥīn
Don't worry, I'll send someone up to look at them now.
B
زين. وأقدر أستخدم النت؟ ما يفتح عندي
zēn. w agdar astakhdim in-nit? ma yiftaḥ ʿindi
Good. And can I use the internet? It won't load for me.
A
أكيد. بعطيك الرقم السري الحين
akīd. baʿṭīk ir-ragam is-sirri l-ḥīn
Of course. I'll give you the password now.
items: we've got our room, we've checked in
istalamt (استلمت) = I received, I picked up
I'm surprised, I found it strange; you were surprised (to a man)
to a woman (you were surprised): istaghrabti (استغربتي)
I'll send someone (to you) (to a man)
to a woman: baṭarrish-lich wāḥid (بطرش لج واحد)
agdar astakhdim …? = can I use …?; also: astaʿmil (أستعمل)
culture: is-samūḥa (minnak) is a polite 'pardon (us)'. Answer ma ʿalēh or masmūḥ, and then say what you need. Keep a complaint calm and short.

title: Checking out
goal: Check out of the hotel and tell the receptionist how your stay went, recycling Forms VII, VIII and X
tip: istānas 'had a good time' is Form X: istānast 'I enjoyed it', istānasna 'we enjoyed it', to a group istānastu? The mistānis you know is its participle. istakhdam 'used' and istaḥmal 'put up with' work the same way: ma istakhdamna shay 'we didn't use anything'.
grammar: recycle: Forms VII, VIII, X (ingiṭaʿ, ishtaghal, niḥtāj, istānas, istakhdam)
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. استانستوا عندنا؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. istānastu ʿindana?
Good morning. Did you enjoy your stay with us?
B
صباح النور. هيه، بس الماي الحار انقطع أمس بعد
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. hē, bas il-māy il-ḥārr ingiṭaʿ ams baʿad
Good morning. Yes, but the hot water went off yesterday as well.
A
آسفين على هالشي. والمكيف؟ اشتغل؟
āsfīn ʿala hash-shay. w il-mkayyif? ishtaghal?
We're sorry about that. And the AC? Did it work?
B
اشتغل، بس استحملت الحر ساعتين!
ishtaghal, bas istaḥmalt il-ḥarr sāʿtēn!
It worked, but I put up with the heat for two hours!
A
السموحة. استخدمتوا شي من الثلاجة؟
is-samūḥa. istakhdamtu shay min ith-thallāja?
Sorry about that. Did you use anything from the fridge?
B
مسموح. لا، ما استخدمنا شي. نحتاج الفاتورة بس
masmūḥ. la, ma istakhdamna shay. niḥtāj il-fātūra bas
That's all right. No, we didn't use anything. We just need the bill.
A
تفضل. وإن شاء الله تزورونا مرة ثانية
tfaẓẓal. w in shāʼ allāh tzūrūna marra thānya
Here you are. And we hope you'll visit us again.
B
إن شاء الله! والله استانسنا
in shāʼ allāh! wallāh istānasna
We will! Honestly, we had a great time.
items: I had a good time, I enjoyed it; you had a good time (to a man)
to a woman (you): istānasti (استانستي); we had a good time: istānasna (استانسنا)
I used; you used (to a man)
to a woman (you used): istakhdamti (استخدمتي); also: istaʿmalt (استعملت)
I put up with (it), I stood it; you put up with (to a man)
to a woman (you put up with): istaḥmalti (استحملتي)
I'm sorry: āsif (a man), āsfa (a woman)
did you have a good time?, did you enjoy it? (to a group)
to one man: istānast? (استانست؟); to one woman: istānasti? (استانستي؟)
to one man: tzūrna (تزورنا); in shāʼ allāh tzūrūna marra thānya = we hope you'll visit us again

title: Checkpoint 3.3: moving day
goal: Checkpoint: Sēf (A) and Fahad help you move into the new flat; ask them for help, sort out the AC and thank them
tip: To a group, a command or a past 'you' ends in -u, and it lengthens before -ni: sāʿdūni 'help me (all of you)', waddūni 'take me'. Group wishes take -kum: allāh ygawwīkum. A plural participle takes -īn: miḥtājīn 'we need, you (all) need'.
grammar: checkpoint 3.3: recycle s3u029–s3u045 (Forms II, III, V, VI, VII, VIII, X)
dialogue: B
يا شباب، ساعدوني شوي في هالكراتين
yā shabāb, sāʿdūni shwayy fi hal-karātīn
Guys, help me a bit with these boxes.
A
أبشر! بس ليش الشقة حارة جي؟ الكهربا انقطعت؟
abshir! bas lēsh ish-shigga ḥārra chī? il-kahraba ingiṭʿat?
Sure! But why's the flat so hot? Has the power gone off?
B
لا، المكيف ما يشتغل. دورت على رقم صاحب الشقة
la, il-mkayyif ma yishtaghil. dawwart ʿala ragam ṣāḥib ish-shigga
No, the AC isn't working. I've been looking for the landlord's number.
A
ولا يهمك. أعرف واحد يصلح مكيفات، بتصل فيه
wala yhimmak. aʿarf wāḥid yṣalliḥ mkayyifāt, battaṣil fīh
Don't worry. I know a guy who fixes ACs; I'll call him.
B
الله يقويكم يا شباب. تعبتوا وايد اليوم
allāh ygawwīkum yā shabāb. tiʿabtu wāyid il-yōm
Thanks for all the work, guys. You've worked so hard today.
A
الله يعافيك، عادي! بس انتو محتاجين ثلاجة أكبر
allāh yʿāfīk, ʿādi! bas intu miḥtājīn thallāja akbar
Thank you, it's nothing! But you and your flatmate need a bigger fridge.
B
صح. ودوني السوق باكر، والغدا علي
ṣaḥḥ. waddūni s-sūg bāchir, w il-ghada ʿalay
True. Take me shopping tomorrow, and lunch is on me.
A
اتفقنا! والله استانسنا وياك اليوم
ittafagna! wallāh istānasna wiyyāk il-yōm
Deal! Honestly, we had a great time with you today.
items: to one man: sāʿidni; to one woman: sāʿdīni
the power's gone off, there's a power cut
God give you strength (to a group, said to people working)
to one man: allāh ygawwīk (الله يقويك)
we need; you (all) need; in need of (a group)
one man: miḥtāj; one woman: miḥtāja
to one man: waddni (ودني); to one woman: waddīni (وديني)
we had a great time with you (to a man)
to a woman: istānasna wiyyāch (استانسنا وياج)
culture: To friends who've worked hard for you, say allāh ygawwīkum (to one man: allāh ygawwīk); a common reply is allāh yʿāfīk.
